turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome in. What brings you to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Well, I'm here because... honestly, it's just wearing me down. For the past year, I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results. And I know what I'm looking at, you know? I'm a phlebotomist, so I draw blood all day. We usually use the lavender top tubes for the CBCs, and the light blue ones for coagulation... actually, the clinic just switched our supplier for the blue tubes last month and the caps are so stiff now, my thumb is constantly bruised from popping them off. It’s ridiculous, they always try to save a few pennies on supplies. 

But anyway, no matter how many doctors or even my own family members tell me his numbers are fine, I just know the chart doesn’t match what I saw. They all just brush me off. My sister says I just need a vacation, which, sure, I haven't been to the beach since before the pandemic, and I do love the ocean, but a trip to Florida isn't going to fix the fact that someone is deliberately messing with his medical records.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed belief that someone is deliberately altering her father's medical records, maintaining this conviction despite contradictory evidence from doctors and family members.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient's speech demonstrates tangentiality, as she wanders off-topic into details about blood draw tubes, suppliers, and her bruised thumb, as well as a tangent about a beach vacation, before returning to her main point.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever heard voices or sounds when no one else was around or that other people couldn't hear?
turns.patient_response:
Voices? No, no, I don't hear anything like that. I mean, my hearing is perfectly fine. Actually, it's almost too good sometimes, because the centrifuge at the clinic makes this terrible high-pitched whining noise. It's one of the older models, and I keep telling my supervisor the motor is going out, but he just won't listen. He just sits in his office all day ordering those cheap blue tubes I told you about. 

And the breakroom fridge has this constant rattle, too. Plus, someone always leaves fish in there. Last Friday it was salmon. Who microwaves salmon in a small medical office? It just lingers in the hallway for hours and gets into your scrubs. I always just bring a turkey wrap, it's so much more considerate of shared spaces. But anyway, no, I don't hear people talking when they aren't there or anything like that. Just regular sounds.

symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly denies hearing voices or people talking when they aren't there.

turns.doctor_question: Outside of this situation with your dad's records, do you often find yourself feeling that friends, family, or coworkers might be dishonest or untrustworthy towards you?
turns.patient_response:
Dishonest? No, not really. I mean, my friends and family are perfectly fine. And I trust my coworkers, for the most part. Well, except Sarah at the front desk, but that's just because she constantly walks off with my favorite pens. Not in a malicious way, she's just so absent-minded. 

I use these very specific black gel pens because they don't smudge on the specimen labels, you know? The ones the clinic provides are those terrible cheap ballpoints that skip right in the middle of writing a patient's date of birth, and then you have to start all over. I actually go to Target to buy my own out of pocket. I was just there on Tuesday to stock up, and they had already put out all the Halloween decorations. Can you believe that? It's barely even September. They had these little ceramic pumpkins that light up, and I almost bought one for the front desk, but then I remembered Sarah taking my pens and figured I'd just keep it for my own apartment. I have this nice little bay window it would look perfect in. My cat loves to sit there and watch the birds. 

But yeah, no, I don't think people are untrustworthy or lying to me in my regular life. It's literally just this one specific situation with my dad's chart, because I know exactly what I saw and they won't admit it. But everyone else is fine.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient reiterates their fixed belief about their father's chart, insisting they know what they saw and that others won't admit it.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangential speech, drifting from the topic of coworkers to gel pens, Target, Halloween decorations, and their cat.
symptom_reasoning.S072: The patient explicitly denies having general negative beliefs or distrust towards others, stating they trust their friends, family, and coworkers.
